chunks: Hadith 5560 — Ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah, from Burayd ibn Muʿāwiyah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man appointed me as his executor, and I asked him to include with me a relative of his, so he did. And the one who appointed me mentioned that he had against the one whom he included with me in the executorship one hundred and fifty dirhams, and with him as collateral for it was a silver cup. Then when the man died, the executor began claiming that he had against him loads of wheat.
He عليه السلام said: If he establishes proof, otherwise he has no right to anything.
He said: I said to him: Is it permissible for him to take anything from what is in his hand? He said: It is not permissible for him.

I said: What do you think—if a man wronged him and took his property, and he was able to take from his property the like of what he took, would that be permissible for him? So he said: Indeed, this is not like that.

key_terms.أَوْصَى: appointed someone as executor and entrusted a bequest
key_terms.حِنْطَةٍ: wheat, here referring to the alleged counterclaim in kind
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: a monetary unit indicating the amount of debt claimed
key_terms.رَهْنٌ: a pledged item held as collateral for a debt
key_terms.لَا يَحِلُّ: it is not lawful or permissible
key_terms.ٱعْتَدَى: wrongfully transgressed against or committed aggression
key_terms.ٱلْبَيِّنَةَ: legal proof or evidentiary confirmation for a claim
key_terms.ٱلْوَصِيَّةِ: the executorship or bequest arrangement over the deceased’s affairs

ai.seo_question: Can an executor take property based on an unproven debt claim in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses a legal dispute involving executorship, debt, and claims made after a person's death. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rules that such a claim must be supported by proof, and without evidence the claimant has no right to take anything from property under his control. The hadith distinguishes this case from directly recovering property wrongfully taken by an oppressor.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5560 - Ibn Faddal narrated from Ali ibn Uqbah from Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

I said to Imam (as): "A man appointed me as his executor, and I asked him to appoint a relative of his to share the responsibility with me, and he agreed. The one who appointed me mentioned that the co-executor owed him one hundred and fifty dirhams and that he had a silver cup as collateral for this debt. When the man passed away, the co-executor began to claim that he was owed sacks of wheat instead."
Abu Abdullah (as), said: "If he brings proof, then his claim is valid; otherwise, he has no right to anything."
I asked: "Is it permissible for him to take anything from what is in his possession?" Imam (as) replied: "It is not permissible for him."

I then asked: "What if someone wrongfully took his wealth, and he found the opportunity to take back from that person's wealth the equivalent of what was taken from him - would that be permissible?" Imam (as) replied: "This is not the same as that."
